subject: Physics
source_note: Compiled from the NTA/NMC NEET UG 2026 syllabus (officially released 8 Jan 2026, largely a continuation of the 2023-24 NCERT-rationalised syllabus) as reported by multiple 2025-2026 coaching/exam-tracker sources, cross-checked Sep 2026. NEET Physics has no separate 'Experimental Skills' unit the way JEE Main does; practicals/experiments are examined inside their parent theory units instead. Always verify against the current-year official NTA/NMC syllabus PDF (neet.nta.nic.in / nmc.org.in) before finalising a question bank, since sub-topic deletions are revised between sessions.
exam_pattern_note: NEET UG Physics: 50 questions printed (Section A: 35 single-correct MCQs, all compulsory; Section B: 15 single-correct MCQs, attempt any 10 - the best 10 attempted are scored). Only single-correct MCQ format is used; NEET has no numerical-value question type (unlike JEE Main Section B) and no multiple-correct or matrix-match formats.

subtopics: Units for measurement, SI units, fundamental and derived units
Dimensional formulae and dimensional analysis
Errors in measurement: absolute, relative, percentage error
Significant figures
topics.syllabus_change_note: 2024-25 rationalisation dropped 'Physics, technology and society' and detailed instrument-accuracy/precision content as separately examinable.

subtopics: Motion in a straight line: position-time and velocity-time graphs, uniform and non-uniform acceleration
Scalars and vectors, vector addition and resolution
Motion in a plane, projectile motion
Uniform circular motion
Newton's three laws of motion and applications
Conservation of linear momentum and its applications
Equilibrium of concurrent forces
Static and kinetic friction, laws of friction
Dynamics of uniform circular motion: centripetal force, banking of roads
topics.syllabus_change_note: Rolling friction dropped as a separately examinable sub-topic in the NCERT-rationalised NEET syllabus.

subtopics: Work done by a constant and a variable force, work-energy theorem
Kinetic and potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy
Elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions
Power

topics.chapter: Motion of System of Particles and Rigid Body
subtopics: Centre of mass of a two-particle system and of a rigid body
Moment of inertia, radius of gyration
Moment of inertia of simple bodies (ring, disc, rod, sphere, cylinder)
Torque, angular momentum and its conservation
Equilibrium of rigid bodies, rolling motion
Universal law of gravitation
Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth
Kepler's laws of planetary motion
Gravitational potential energy and gravitational potential, escape velocity
Orbital velocity of a satellite
Elastic behaviour, stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law, Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity
Pressure in a fluid, Pascal's law, buoyancy
Surface tension, surface energy, angle of contact, capillary rise
Viscosity, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, streamline flow, Bernoulli's theorem
Heat, temperature, thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, calorimetry, change of state, heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation)
topics.syllabus_change_note: Poisson's ratio and Reynolds number dropped as separately examinable items in the rationalised syllabus.

subtopics: Thermal equilibrium, zeroth law of thermodynamics
Heat, work, internal energy, first law of thermodynamics
Isothermal and adiabatic processes
Second law of thermodynamics, reversible and irreversible processes
Heat engines and refrigerators (qualitative)
topics.syllabus_change_note: Detailed Carnot-cycle efficiency derivation trimmed to qualitative treatment in the rationalised syllabus.

topics.chapter: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory
subtopics: Equation of state of a perfect gas, work done in compressing a gas
Kinetic theory assumptions, concept of pressure
Kinetic interpretation of temperature, rms speed
Degrees of freedom, law of equipartition of energy, specific heats of gases
Mean free path, Avogadro's number
Periodic motion, simple harmonic motion (SHM) and its equation
Simple pendulum, spring-mass system, energy in SHM
Wave motion: longitudinal and transverse, speed of a travelling wave
Superposition of waves, standing waves in strings and organ pipes
Beats
topics.syllabus_change_note: Doppler effect in sound and forced/damped-oscillation derivations dropped as separately examinable items in the NEET rationalised syllabus.

subtopics: Coulomb's law, electric field, field lines, electric dipole and dipole field
Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field
Electric flux, Gauss's law and applications (line charge, sheet, spherical shell)
Electric potential, potential due to a point charge and a dipole, equipotential surfaces
Capacitance, parallel-plate capacitor with dielectric, capacitors in series/parallel, energy stored
topics.syllabus_change_note: Van de Graaff generator dropped as a separately examinable sub-topic.

subtopics: Electric current, drift velocity, Ohm's law
Resistance, resistivity, temperature dependence
Series and parallel combinations of resistors and cells
Kirchhoff's laws, Wheatstone bridge, metre bridge
Potentiometer (basic principle and simple applications only)
topics.syllabus_change_note: Detailed potentiometer-comparison-of-emfs derivations trimmed; qualitative principle and simple application remain examinable.

topics.chapter: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
subtopics: Biot-Savart law and Ampere's law, applications to straight wire, loop and solenoid
Force on a moving charge and on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
Torque on a current loop, moving-coil galvanometer and conversion to ammeter/voltmeter
Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, basic magnetic properties of materials
topics.syllabus_change_note: Cyclotron and Oersted's experiment dropped as separately examinable items.

subtopics: Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, Lenz's law
Self-inductance and mutual inductance
Alternating currents, peak and rms values
AC circuit with series LCR combination, resonance, power factor
AC generator and transformer
Displacement current (qualitative)
Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics, transverse nature
Electromagnetic spectrum and typical uses of its bands
Reflection and refraction at plane and spherical surfaces, mirror and lens formulae, total internal reflection
Thin lens formula, lens maker's formula, power of a lens, combination of lenses
Refraction through a prism, dispersion
Wave nature of light, Huygens' principle
Young's double-slit interference, single-slit diffraction
Polarisation, Brewster's law, Polaroids
topics.syllabus_change_note: Detailed optical-instrument (microscope/telescope) magnifying-power derivations reduced/dropped as separately examinable line items.

topics.chapter: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
subtopics: Photoelectric effect, Einstein's photoelectric equation
Particle nature of light: the photon
Matter waves, de Broglie relation
Alpha-particle scattering, Rutherford's model, Bohr model, energy levels, hydrogen spectrum
Composition and size of the nucleus, mass-energy relation, mass defect
Binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number
Radioactivity: alpha, beta, gamma decay
Nuclear fission and fusion
Energy bands in solids (qualitative): conductors, insulators, semiconductors
p-n junction diode, I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias
Diode as a rectifier
LED, photodiode, solar cell, Zener diode as a voltage regulator
Logic gates (OR, AND, NOT, NAND, NOR) and truth tables
topics.syllabus_change_note: Transistor amplifier/oscillator circuit analysis dropped; qualitative diode and logic-gate behaviour remains examinable.
